newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand share market rallies on favourable MPS.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand share market rallies on favourable MPS.

text.p: The New Zealand share market basked in the afterglow of a favourable monetary policy statement from the Reserve Bank on Friday, described by one broker as a "win, win" for equities.
By late morning, the NZSE-40 Capital Index was up 20.52 points at 2,430.68.
But trade was thin, with turnover exaggerated by some large crossings in Telecom, Tranz Rail and Brierley Investments.

The Reserve Bank earlier sanctioned an easing of conditions and eluded to another small easing in the December quarter, which led to a sharp sell off in the New Zealand dollar and a rally in interest rate markets.
"The market is enjoying the positive tone set by the MPS," Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said.
"It's received the news very warmly as it should, so to see it up 20 points is no great surprise," he said.
"It's a win, win situation for most companies," Patterson said.
Stocks with good domestic exposure were the main beneficiaries of the new monetary environment, among them being Independent Newspapers, up 20 at NZ$7.60, and Fletcher Building, up 12 at NZ$4.45.
